insight: Recent rain (15 mm over the past few days) is washing urban runoff into the surf — the single biggest cause of beach contamination — especially near storm drains and creek mouths. The model's main signals right now: 15 mm of rain has fallen, washing bacteria-laden runoff into the surf; limited sunlight is raising risk (less UV to disinfect the water); and elevated river/creek flow is raising risk by carrying watershed runoff to the shore. There's no recent lab sample to anchor this (the last was 32 days ago), so the estimate is based entirely on current environmental conditions. It's a naturally clean, well-flushed open-coast beach (unsafe only ~3% of the time), so outside of storms it's reliably safe.
